ACCEPTThe corrected note resolves the gaps identified in my first review. The original coordinates are now justified, and I find no remaining mathematical gap in the exclusive-strip lemma, the exact scalar optimization and relaxation, or the all- $p$ /all- $k$  construction, under the stated prescribed-source dependencies and whole-receiver ledger.This verdict concerns the corrected note supplied here. It does not use the reported finite controls, Lean results, or other review statuses as premises.1. The complete support template closes the geometric gapThe revised distance-three argument in §4 is correct.For  $i<j$ , put  $d=j-i$ . The facing chamber-row separation is
$$R_j-(R_i+1)=4d-1.$$
Arm-to-arm and later-chamber-to-earlier-arm separations are at least  $4d$ ; an earlier chamber and a later arm have vertical separation at least  $4d+1$ . Consequently, endpoint distance three occurs only when  $j=i+1$ , between
$$(R_i+1,z),\qquad (R_i+4,z)$$
in a common column.Every prescribed support lies one step from its assigned endpoint. If supports belonging to different  $H_i$  were adjacent, their assigned endpoints would therefore be at distance at most three. In the only possible distance-three case, the endpoint–support–support–endpoint path must be the straight vertical path, placing the supports at
$$(R_i+2,z),\qquad (R_i+3,z).$$
But  $H_{i+1}$  starts at row  $R_i+4$ , and the complete template has no support above its origin row. The second required support cannot exist.This proves the missing compatibility for every  $p$ , while retaining the original coordinates. Endpoint distance at least three also excludes support coincidence and a support acquiring a foreign endpoint neighbor.The displayed template itself is consistent with the required local feasibility: the outer and inner arm supports alternate as stated, the axial supports are separated from the neighboring side supports, and every selected support has its own endpoint as its unique occupied neighbor within the individual source. In particular, the missing row above the chamber is a property of the complete template, not an assumption inferred from finite examples.2. The remaining all- $p$  geometry is validThe other interfaces have sufficient separation or the necessary explicit parity check. $K$  versus the  $H_i$ . The last  $H_i$  chamber ends at row  $4p-1$ , whereas  $K$ 's first chamber endpoint is at  $4p+5$ . The innermost arm columns are  $4p-1$  and  $4p+26$ , while  $K$ 's endpoint columns lie between  $4p+6$  and  $4p+12$ . These give the required separation for endpoints and their one-step supports.The comb versus the innermost arm. On odd rows, the relevant source and comb side-support columns are  $c-2$  and  $c+1$ ; on even rows they are  $c-4$  and  $c-1$ . The potentially dangerous same-row pair  $c-2,c-1$  cannot occur because its two supports require opposite row parities. Across consecutive rows, the nearest pair has distance two. The lower axial comb support is also at distance two from the closest source support; the upper axial support is farther away.The comb lies within the portion of the arm where this parity formula applies. Its endpoints and axial supports occupy rows
$$8p+4,\ldots,8p+9,$$
whereas the innermost arm runs from row  $4p$  through  $12p+4$ . The needed support positions are therefore available for every  $p\ge2$ , including  $p=2$ .The comb versus  $K$ . Their endpoints are separated by at least four, which is sufficient to exclude adjacency between their one-step supports.These checks establish feasibility and separation of the endpoint components. The established retained-support freezing results can consequently be applied to those components.Crossings and the baseline lossThe horizontal mouths have distinct physical row bands. Their intersections with  $K$ 's vertical mouth are exactly
$$[t_i,t_i+1]\times[4p+12,4p+13].$$
Since
$$8p+8\le t_i\le12p+4,$$
every such tile lies strictly inside  $K$ 's mouth.These tiles are at least thirteen columns from every  $H_i$  arm and well below the chambers. They are at least five from the relevant  $K$  endpoints, and the comb is separated from them horizontally. Thus no endpoint or prescribed support occupies a crossing tile in the displayed baseline. Each has actual deficit two, giving
$$X=p,\qquad K_{\mathrm{loss}}=2p.$$
The coordinates, including all supports, fit the stated rectangle: their row and column bounds are contained in
$$[2,12p+11]\times[2,8p+23],$$
inside the prescribed  $(12p+18)\times(8p+30)$  rectangle.3. The end labels and completion quantifier are now sufficientThe sparse-end forcing argument is valid for both kinds of additional occupied vertices:Occupying  $(t,c+1)$  would give the retained support  $(t-1,c+1)$  a second occupied neighbor.Occupying  $(t+1,c+1)$  would give the retained axial support  $(t+1,c)$  a second occupied neighbor.Thus neither a new selected vertex nor a new matching endpoint can occupy those corners. The saturated singleton’s remaining corner is similarly forced blank by its two retained supports.The added completion restriction closes the earlier quantifier gap. Retaining the listed components with their matching and supports, while excluding additional endpoint components meeting  $G$ , fixes the mouth end incidences. Additional feasible selections can change actual deficits, but the same conservative strip lower bounds remain applicable.For this family, the sparse end belongs to  $H_0$ 's strip alone and the saturated end belongs to no mouth. The corrected definitions therefore give, consistently,
$$F=-1,\qquad O=1,\qquad J=0.$$
There is no confusion between union membership and strip multiplicity in this calculation.4. The strengthened strip identity and physical accounting are correctThe revised proof of the per-strip count uses the granted global conservation exactly as needed:
$$L_i\le2b_i-2,\qquad
\sum_iL_i=\sum_i(2b_i-2)
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
L_i=2b_i-2$$
for every strip.It follows that
$$D_i=2b_i+f_i+a_i+d_i'
   \ge \max(0,2b_i+f_i)=q_i.$$
For an independent set in the full physical-intersection graph, the selected strips have disjoint physical tile sets. Hence
$$D_G\ge\sum_{i\in I}D_i\ge q(I),$$
and the granted ledger yields
$$\Delta\ge q(I)-B+R.$$
The optional edge-deletion qualification is now correctly uniform over the completion class. Such a deletion is justified only when the shared tiles contribute zero donor weight throughout that class.No source endpoint, comb end, matching export, or shifted square is separately spent. The proof uses actual original no- $P$  deficits and retains  $R$  once.5. The exact optimization and relaxed-model optimality remain validThe weighted cover–cut correspondence proves
$$W=\sum_iq_i-\operatorname{mincut}.$$
The added feasible edge-flow witness resolves the previous distinction between a certified lower bound and a certified optimum. Nonnegative edge flows satisfying the incident capacity bound at each vertex determine a feasible full network flow. Equality of the flow value and the cover/cut weight then certifies optimality.The relaxed-model proof also remains exact. An independent set bounds every feasible relaxed resource assignment below by its weight. Conversely, for a maximum flow of value  $v$ , the shared resources cost  $v$ , and the nonnegative private residuals cost
$$\sum_iq_i-2v.$$
The total is
$$\sum_iq_i-v=W.$$
Thus  $W$  is attained in both the real relaxation and the integral model.For the displayed star, an explicit optimality witness is immediate: the center is a cover of weight two, and one unit sent through each of two leaf-center edges gives a feasible flow of value two. Since the total vertex weight is  $2p+1$ ,
$$W=2p+1-2=2p-1.$$
This is a classical max-flow application with the scope claimed in the note.6. The family gives all the advertised comparisonsFor one star,
$$B=p+1,\qquad
q(H_0)=1,\qquad q(H_i)=2\ (i\ge1),\qquad q(K)=2.$$
Therefore
$$W=2p-1\ge p+1=B$$
for every  $p\ge2$ , and more precisely
$$\Delta\ge p-2+R.$$
For the all- $k$  construction, the original  $42\times46$  and  $46\times42$  containing rectangles fit the  $50\times50$  blocks with the stated margins. The even translations preserve physical-tile alignment. The margins prevent interblock endpoint/support adjacency, physical mouth intersections, and adjacent parallel mouths that could coalesce across blocks.Consequently,
$$B=3k,\qquad F=-k,\qquad W=3k.$$
Selecting the leaves in every star uses globally disjoint physical strip sets and proves
$$\Delta\ge R\ge0.$$
Thus the corrected family does give arbitrarily negative  $F$ , together with the coefficient-one bound, without duplicated physical resources.Its baselines also lie outside both stated earlier sufficient conditions:
$$F=-k<0,$$
and
$$K_{\mathrm{loss}}+O=4k+k=5k>3k=B+J.$$
The latter comparison is correctly restricted to the baseline; allowed extra selections can change actual crossing deficits.Finally, componentwise direction selection is strictly stronger than the best single global direction in the alternating family. The component directional totals alternate between  $(3,2)$  and  $(2,3)$ , so
$$\text{best global-direction weight}
=\frac{5k+(k\bmod2)}2,$$
whereas the componentwise certificate gives  $3k$ . Its gain is exactly
$$\boxed{\left\lfloor\frac{k}{2}\right\rfloor},$$
which is positive for every  $k\ge2$ .The note appropriately limits these comparisons to the conservative structural certificate and leaves the unrestricted grid problem open. No further geometric repair is required for the corrected note.
